# JustDukkan

> JustDukkan, LLC builds custom AI agent teams. For each client we design a hierarchical (hub-and-spoke) agentic system around their own processes: an orchestrator that plans and routes, specialist agents with bounded scope, MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, typed tools and skills, connected to the client's existing systems through their APIs, and then kept running with regular maintenance. We do not resell off-the-shelf agents or generic agent subscriptions; every system is built for the client and belongs to the client. Based in Delaware, USA; we work with companies internationally in English and Turkish.

## What we do

- **Agent Team Design** — turn a real process into agent roles: an orchestrator that plans, routes and verifies, specialist agents with one bounded job each, explicit scope and authority limits, and the points where a person decides.
- **Build & Deployment** — write the agents, the typed tools they call and the skills that carry the client's procedures; take the team into production one capability at a time, with evaluations at every step.
- **Integrations: API & MCP** — connect the team to the systems the client already runs: API integrations (CRM, ERP, ticketing, internal tools) and MCP servers that expose only what each agent is allowed to touch, with auth, audit logs and approval gates.
- **Operate & Maintain** — keep a live agent team working: evaluation sets kept current, regression checks when a model or an API changes, new tools and skills as scope grows, and monitoring for cost, latency and failures.

We build custom agent teams. We do not resell off-the-shelf agents or connect clients to someone else's agent subscription.

## Expertise

Hub-and-spoke orchestration · MCP servers & tool design · Agent skills & instructions (versioned, tested) · API & system integration (CRM/ERP, ticketing, messaging, internal tools; auth, retries, idempotency) · Knowledge & retrieval (RAG) pipelines · Evaluation & guardrails · Cloud architecture (AWS, Google Cloud) · Cost & operations (token budgets, model routing, caching, monitoring)

We design for the models companies already use: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, Mistral, Llama, Qwen, Grok.

## How we work

1. Discover — map the process with the people who do the work and separate the steps that need judgment from the ones that do not.
2. Design the agent team — roles, scope and authority per agent, the tools and MCP servers each one calls, the data it sees, and the human decision points.
3. Build and integrate — agents, typed tools, skills and MCP servers written and wired into the client's APIs, shipped agent by agent with evals and human checkpoints.
4. Operate — monitoring, documentation and training, then regular maintenance: evaluations, model and API updates, new capabilities as scope grows.

Outcomes we design for: a system shaped like the client's process rather than a generic tool; work the agent team runs end to end with people on exceptions and decisions; a maintained system rather than a project that ages.

## Engagement

No packages and no price list. We look at a process, design the agent team it needs and decide together with the client whether it is worth building. Maintenance is agreed separately once a system is live. Start with a Solution Consultation call: https://cal.com/justdukkan/solution-consultation

## Insights (articles)

- [Designing the agent team: roles, scope and handoffs](https://justdukkan.com/insights/designing-the-agent-team/) — Before any code is written, an agentic system is a set of decisions about roles: which agents exist, what each one may read and change, where it must stop, and how work moves between them.
- [Hub-and-spoke agent architecture: how to build multi-agent systems that stay explainable](https://justdukkan.com/insights/hub-and-spoke-agent-architecture/) — A hub-and-spoke architecture puts one orchestrator in charge of planning, routing and verification, and gives every specialist agent, tool and human reviewer a bounded job.
- [Agent team topologies: which hierarchy to build, and when](https://justdukkan.com/insights/agent-topologies/) — Hub-and-spoke is a good default, not the only shape.
- [Designing MCP servers and tools that agents can use safely](https://justdukkan.com/insights/mcp-server-and-tool-design/) — MCP gives agents a standard way to call tools, but a badly designed tool is still a badly designed tool.
- [Connecting agents to your APIs: identity, idempotency and the failures nobody plans for](https://justdukkan.com/insights/connecting-agents-to-your-apis/) — An agent team is only as good as its connection to the systems that hold the work.
- [Agent skills: packaging repeatable expertise so agents stop improvising](https://justdukkan.com/insights/agent-skills/) — A tool is something an agent can do.
- [Delegate to human: making escalation a first-class capability](https://justdukkan.com/insights/delegate-to-human/) — Approval gates are planned.
- [Human-in-the-loop for agentic systems: where people belong, and where they only slow things down](https://justdukkan.com/insights/human-in-the-loop-for-agentic-systems/) — "Keep a human in the loop" is easy to say and usually done badly: either every step waits for someone, or nothing does.
- [Operating agentic systems: what maintenance actually means](https://justdukkan.com/insights/operating-agentic-systems/) — A live agent team is not a finished project.
- [From manual process to automated flow: an architecture playbook](https://justdukkan.com/insights/process-automation-architecture/) — Most automation projects fail before the first model call, in the mapping and the boundaries.

## Open source

- [invoice-intake-mcp](https://github.com/justdukkan/invoice-intake-mcp) — reference MCP servers for supplier invoice intake: read/draft/commit split, typed errors, server-side approval gate, audit log, replayable evals. On PyPI (`uvx invoice-intake-mcp`) and the official MCP Registry as `com.justdukkan/invoice-intake-mcp`.
